name: Atlantic coasts and northern / western inland lakes — format: tools/spots/README.md
Malo-les-Bains (Dunkerque)
notes: Dunkerque Flysurfing Club beach; very wide at low tide. Also: Bray-Dunes 12 km east (huge flat beach by the Belgian border).

name: Les Hemmes de Marck
notes: Very wide gently sloping beach, flattish water behind sandbanks; best in NW to NE winds. Also: Calais – Blériot-Plage 8 km west; Gravelines – Petit-Fort-Philippe 12 km east (flat petite mer at high tide).

name: Wissant
notes: Between the two capes (venturi): powerful wind and waves, experienced riders. Also: Sangatte 10 km north-east (windiest of the Côte d'Opale), Wimereux – Pointe aux Oies 12 km south (waves).

name: Le Touquet
notes: Launch north of Aqualud; the Canche bay works in E winds around high tide (strong currents). Also: Hardelot 14 km north (low-tide pools), Berck-sur-Mer 14 km south (huge beach, flat pools at low tide).

name: Le Crotoy
notes: Tidal bay: rideable around high tide only. Do not cross the yellow buoys of the nature reserve. Also: Cayeux-sur-Mer – La Mollière on the sea side of the bay (all tides).

name: Quiberville
notes: Marked kite zone (mandatory); works WSW to NW. Pebble beach, sand at low tide.

name: Merville-Franceville
notes: Dedicated kite zone at the west end of Boulevard Wattier, open all year (the only kite beach in July–August). Keep out of the bird reserve at the Orne estuary to the west. Also: Ouistreham – Riva-Bella 5 km west (low tide only).

name: Utah Beach
notes: Huge beach; best at low to mid tide.

name: Agon-Coutainville
notes: Also: Gouville-sur-Mer 10 km north.

name: Cherrueix
notes: Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel: huge tidal range; ride around high tide.

name: Lancieux
notes: Flat, shallow bay; best at low tide. July–August: Saint-Sieu beach is closed, launch at Tête de Chien (low tide) or Roche Morin (high tide). Also: Saint-Malo – Le Sillon 12 km east (urban, summer launch zone).

name: Hillion – Bon Abri
notes: Bay of Saint-Brieuc: huge tidal range, ride mid to high tide. Nature reserve nearby. Also: Plérin – Les Rosaires across the bay for easterly winds.

name: Saint-Michel-en-Grève (Lieue de Grève)
notes: Huge 4 km sandy beach, no rocks, gentle waves: the easiest place in the area to learn. The sea goes out up to 3 km at low tide (long walk to the water, then a vast flat standing-depth area). Kite's Cool school on the beach (March to November). Saint-Efflam, at the west end, is the same beach.

name: Santec – Le Dossen
notes: Waves; best in S to SW wind, works N to S. In westerlies the inshore water is blocked at high tide: ride low tide. Rocks, all visible. Bathing zone in summer (about 1 June to 15 September, one blog, no town text found): keep clear of swimmers. Green algae in summer at the south river mouth. Kite Sans Frontière teaches here.

name: Keremma
notes: The reference spot of North Finistère: 5 km of beach between the Kernic and Goulven bays, FFVL-labelled and looked after by the Finistère Kite Association. Flat lagoon-like water at low tide (about 500 m of launch space), choppy at high tide. Best in NW wind (NW to NE works). Rocks and a strong current at the river mouth. Dunes are Natura 2000: stay on the paths. The Goulven bird reserve on the west side is closed to all boats. Lifeguards in summer only. Also: Guissény – Le Vougot 10 km west.

name: Pentrez
notes: Long west-facing beach on the Bay of Douarnenez (about 4 km of sand at low tide, 2.5 km at high tide); waves, side-shore in S to SW winds. Kite zone listed by the beach directories; kite school West Gliss in Saint-Nic. Rip currents are reported on the beach.

name: La Torche
notes: Kiters launch north of the point (towards Tronoën), away from the surfers; waves. Intermediate to expert; currents in the water, rocks only near the point. Kite schools at Plomeur (Twentynine, CEKB). Check the beach signs. Also: Tronoën 1.5 km north (kite zone about 300 m south of the car park; current towards the bunker at high tide).

name: Mousterlin
notes: West of the Pointe de Mousterlin; shown as a kite zone on the beach page and in the Brittany tourism board's list of kite spots; an association teaches here. Also: Bénodet – Lagune du Letty 2.5 km west (flat-water lagoon behind the dune spit).

name: Gâvres
notes: Ocean beach (Grande Plage, waves, sideshore in W winds, best around mid tide: shorebreak at high tide) or the flat, shallow Petite Mer de Gâvres from mid tide. Tide decides where you can ride, and part of the area is a military zone: follow the signs. Also: Le Linès 5 km east on the same sandbar; Fort-Bloqué 11 km west (waves).

name: Penthièvre
notes: Bay side of the Penthièvre isthmus (flat water, oyster shells) and ocean side. Ride from 3 h before to 3 h after low tide only. Late May–mid September (29 May–11 Sep in the school and guide sources): bay side banned; on the ocean side take off and land only in the marked zones (north sector, accesses 10–11; Pouladen, posts 1–2, experienced riders). April 2026: the Saint-Pierre-Quiberon mayor said she is considering banning kites on some beaches from summer 2026: check the town hall. Also: Plouharnel – Les Sables Blancs 2 km north on the bay side (NE to SE winds); Erdeven – Kerhillio 8 km north (ocean).

name: Assérac – Pont-Mahé
notes: Shallow bay on the Assérac / Pénestin border, you can stand almost everywhere: the place to learn in Loire-Atlantique. SW to W wind (W is best), thermal breezes. The bay dries out at low tide and the launch area shrinks at high tide, check the tide table. A yellow-buoy zone keeps swimmers apart in summer. Kite school on the beach.

name: La Baule
notes: Plage Benoît and the bay: flat banks at low to mid tide, W to SE wind, choppy at high tide. 15 June to 15 September (period when the channels are buoyed): no kiting from the beach; experienced riders only, through the K13 channel at the Pornichet border (no schools), opened by the lifeguards, wind above 6 knots and enough wet sand (Pornichet order ARR2026-212). Outside that period it is free, at your own risk.

name: Notre-Dame-de-Monts
notes: Wide beach at low tide. Also: Fromentine 7 km north (flat channel facing Noirmoutier, 2 h either side of low tide).

name: La Tranche-sur-Mer
notes: Plage du Phare, facing Île de Ré: waves, wind and current, good level needed, crowded on thermal days. Local guides: May to September the only beach where kiting is allowed (not found in an official text, check the town hall); off season most beaches, but never Belle Henriette. Parking fills up early.

name: Île de Ré – Rivedoux
notes: North beach (bridge to the esplanade), partly reserved for kitesurfing; sheltered from waves, shallow, school on the beach. Works NW to NE (guides). Oyster beds cut the space at low tide, so best from mid to high tide. Stay away from the bridge. Summer limits are set by the town hall: check the buoyed zone.

name: Châtelaillon-Plage
notes: Kite area south of the main beach, in front of the sea wall; two blue flags mark it in summer and it is restricted then (check the town hall). Flat at low tide with rocks offshore, good riding at high tide. School on site. Exposed to swell.

name: Oléron – Plage des Huttes
notes: 5 km beach, windy all year, sheltered from the open ocean; works S to NW and most of all in NW wind (Seulières end). Flat at low tide, shore break at high tide, beach narrows at high tide. A kite zone is set aside in summer (blue flags) and the town hall limits hours: check before riding. Rocks and currents on big tides; schools on the beach.

name: La Palmyre – Bonne Anse
notes: Sheltered shallow bay with a muddy bottom, school on the esplanade. Works in every wind except N and NE. Ride the rising tide, about 2 h either side of high water; strong currents when the bay empties.

name: Lac d'Hourtin-Carcans
notes: Big flat-water lake, launch at Hourtin Port on the east shore. State rules (prefectoral order of 1 Sept 2014): kiting only from 15 November to 31 March, north of the Pointe Blanche – Lacanau channel line, away from the shore strip; the town map shows a kite zone. Check with the schools before a summer session.

name: Lac de Lacanau
notes: Flat, shallow lake with schools at Le Moutchic. Kiting is allowed only in the marked zones either side of the channel to the Talaris marina (prefectoral order of 1 Sept 2014). Also: Lacanau-Océan 7 km west for waves.

name: Bassin d'Arcachon – Claouey
notes: Tidal basin, 2–3 h either side of high tide; muddy bottom, oyster shells. Closed July–August. Also: Andernos (Le Bétey), La Hume and Les Arbousiers elsewhere on the basin.

name: Lac de Cazaux – Navarrosse
notes: Flat, shallow lake (Cazaux-Sanguinet), south shore. Navarrosse launch September–May; June–August use the kite zone at Mayotte (just east). Also: Port de l'Estey (Sanguinet) on the same lake.

name: Mimizan
notes: Plage Sud kite zone; keep away from the river mouth currents.

name: Anglet – La Madrague
notes: Waves, experienced riders. Allowed November–May; in season only early morning and after 19:00 via the marked channel. Also: Hendaye (only Basque beach without cliffs, banned in July–August).

name: Lac du Der – Giffaumont
notes: Kite zone regulated by the local club (KDA); red zone closed 15 June–15 September.

name: Crozon – Goulien
notes: Waves; main kite beach of the Crozon peninsula. Crescent beach of the Anse de Dinan, less exposed to swell than La Palue, so riders come here in strong wind or big swell. NE is the wave-kite wind; avoid W wind with a big swell; at low tide you slalom between rocks. Also: Kersiguénou in the middle of the crescent, for S winds.

name: Île-Tudy
notes: Plage du Sillon: at low tide rocks in the middle of the beach make a shallow lagoon you can stand in; strong S winds at high tide give waves and shorebreak. Works E to SW. Crowded with sunbathers in summer; the beach is lifeguarded 1 July–31 August, 13:00–19:00. A midday summer kite ban is reported but no official text was found: check the signs or the town hall.

name: Bénodet – Lagune du Letty
notes: Flat-water lagoon (Mer Blanche) behind the dune spit; riders launch at the slipway below the UCPA. Works only in southerly winds and only around high tide (the lagoon dries out at low water, strong tidal currents): go with a local instructor the first time. Plenty of room beyond the sandbar. Natura 2000 site.

name: Crozon – Kersiguénou
notes: Middle of the Anse de Dinan crescent, 1 km from Goulien: riders move here (or to Kerloc'h in the north) when the wind turns south. More sheltered from swell than La Palue, so a fallback in strong wind or swell. Waves; rocks at low tide.

name: Crozon – Morgat
notes: Sheltered beach of Morgat bay, in the lee of the cliffs; listed with a kite zone by the beach directory. Very busy with swimmers in summer: check the signs and the lifeguard flags.

name: Plonévez-Porzay – Kervel
notes: Wide, flat beach on the east side of the Bay of Douarnenez, listed as a kite zone. Best in southerly winds (cliffs to the north make other winds gusty); often freeride only, waves cleaner than at Pentrez. Campsite holidaymakers fill the beach in summer.

name: Pouldreuzic – Penhors
notes: Long sandy beach of the Bay of Audierne with a nautical centre on the beach; listed as a kite zone, and the sand-yacht school Plein Ouest rents kite gear. Known mostly for surf: waves and rip currents, check the flags.

name: Plouhinec – Mesperleuc'h
notes: Beach used by kiters and freeriders on flat days; with swell it is a mushy beach break. Lots of room and, according to the kite guide, no restrictions.

name: Le Ster
notes: Wide south-facing sandy beach (almost 4 km) facing the Étocs islets; beginners and bump-and-jump riders. W to SW winds are cross-shore. Reef on the right, shallow at low tide. The kite guide says kiting is banned in the daytime during summer thermal winds: no official text found, check the signs.

name: Trégunc – Kersidan
notes: Croissant-shaped sandy beach, a fallback when the west-coast swell is too heavy; intermediate to expert, small shorebreak around high water. The kite guide says kiting is banned in high summer: no official text found, check the signs. Grass to rig on, parking.

name: Fort-Bloqué
notes: Long beach (1.5–2 km) open to the south-west, waves; kiters share it with surfers (surf school at the Pen er Malo car park), busy in good wind. Lifeguards in July and August; check the beach flags. Guidel kite rules: see the Lorient tourist office.

name: Erdeven – Kerhillio
notes: Reference spot of the area (schools on the beach: Rêve de Glisse, You Kite). Ride from 3 h before to 3 h after low tide. Tourist office: kite zone in the south-east part of the beach, beyond the yellow buoys, marked all year. In high season the zone is the east sector (posts 27–28): take off and land only, then go beyond 300 m; at high tide it is discouraged and not allowed from 3 h before to 3 h after high water at coefficients above 85.

name: Plouharnel – Les Sables Blancs
notes: Bay side of the Quiberon isthmus for NE to SE winds; wide beach, the only unrestricted kite spot of the bay according to the guides. Best at low to mid tide, choppy higher up (the little La Piscine bay to the north only works at high tide). Avoid the oyster parks (poles, yellow buoys ~500 m out); wear booties.

name: La Turballe – Pen Bron
notes: Ocean side north of the Croisic roadstead: freeride and bump-and-jump, strong shore break at high tide, little beach left at high tide (sea wall). One guide says kiting is strictly banned here in summer: no official text found, check the town hall before going. Conservatoire du littoral and Natura 2000 land, naturist beach. No kite school.

name: Saint-Michel-Chef-Chef – Tharon

name: Saint-Jean-de-Monts – Estacade
notes: Base nautique on the Estacade beach teaches kitesurf with a supervised navigation zone; respect the zone and wear a life jacket. Lifeguards 1 July to 31 August. One source only: ask the base for the rules and best wind.

name: Saint-Hilaire-de-Riez – Les Becs
notes: Kite zone south of the Salins beach, between Les Salins and Les Becs (tourist office). Do not launch from the Salins naturist beach, which has a lifeguard post in summer. Kite school nearby (Saint Gilles Kite School, FFVL). No official text found, check the town hall.

name: Les Sables-d'Olonne – Grande Plage

name: Le Veillon
